# /maintain

## Kit upkeep (default)

Inspect instructions, reviewers, policy, agents, skills and templates for duplication,
contradictions and stale references. Keep core instructions short; procedures belong in
on-demand files. Compare behavior with the hook manual before promising enforcement.
Run the kit's documented validation commands if this is the starter repository.

Refresh project context only with established facts. In the starter itself,
`.claude/context/project-context.md` is a blank shipping template; leave it blank and use
root instructions and the starter's `docs-vault/` for kit-specific knowledge.

## `/maintain project`

1. Detect — for existing application code, map stack, tests and architecture. A large repo
   may justify independent read-only agents. An empty project uses `/start`.
2. Adopt — when setup is incomplete, merge the shared-workflow reference into existing project instructions;
   preserve user rules. Establish context/docs and configure the actual test and formatter
   commands. An existing instruction file alone does not prove Conductor is configured.
3. Audit — inspect structure, reuse, test gaps and relevant security/performance/accessibility
   risks. Use specialists only for independently useful questions. Prioritize evidence.
4. Apply — if the user requested implementation of an agreed plan, proceed. Otherwise present
   the concrete proposed changes for approval. Keep refactors small and behavior-preserving,
   with existing or characterization tests protecting the affected behavior.
5. Report — changes, verification and deferred findings. Update docs as part of the work.

Respect prior authorization and human intent. Adding files or agents requires a recurring
need; do not introduce more machinery just to reduce a theoretical token cost.
